payout_quote: Charge a 10-cent deposit on eligible drink containers. / Refund the full deposit up to $25 per day per person.
steps: Buy eligible beverages in Michigan (10¢ deposit charged at checkout)
Keep the empty containers (same brand/size/type the store sells, clean)
Return them to a retailer during normal business hours (machines or hand count)
Receive the 10¢-per-container refund (up to $25 per day per person per store)
catches: This returns YOUR OWN deposit money paid at purchase — it is recovering your own money, not new income.
Only containers bought in-state with the correct deposit label are redeemable; out-of-state containers are ineligible and redeeming them is fraud.
Refund capped at $25 per day per person; stores may refuse containers they don't sell or that are very dirty.
biggest_catch: Returns your own 10¢ deposit — you paid it at purchase. This is deposit recovery, not income.
eligibility: Anyone who purchased eligible returnable containers in Michigan.
timing: Refund paid at return, during store hours.

c1.evidence: Michigan.gov official consumer-protection page plus MCL 445.571 (10¢ refund value in statute); state sources.

c2.evidence: Official michigan.gov page: stores must charge 10-cent deposit and refund the full deposit up to $25/day/person.

c3.evidence: No fee to return; deposit already paid at purchase.

c4.evidence: 10¢ cash refund per container, max $25/day/person; stores must accept same brand/size/type they sell.

s1.note: Purchased eligible containers in Michigan; containers clean and of brands the store sells.

s5.note: michigan.gov — official State of Michigan page.

s6.note: Steps are concrete: buy, save empties, return to retailer, get refund.

notes: Highest deposit in the US (10¢); strict daily cap limits batch size.
numeric_basis: payout from official michigan.gov terms (10¢/container); time: sorting empties + store return trip est. 15–45 min active.
